signal: AirOps raised a $40M Series B led by Greylock and plans to more than double headcount and expand into Europe

email.body1:
Nick, saw AirOps closed a $40M Series B led by Greylock and is planning to more than double headcount and expand into Europe.

Scaling pipeline that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before the new reps ramp, and that is where deals quietly go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for AirOps off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nick, quick follow-up for AirOps.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can, especially as you open Europe. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings AirOps needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Nick, last bit of proof for AirOps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how AirOps' reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nick, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and the raise-to-international-expansion stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-B motion? I'll tailor it to AirOps either way.
